steps.text: Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Place the eggs, milk, vanilla extract, sugar, salt, and flour into a blender. Pulse until no dry lumps remain in the batter. Melt the butter in an 8-inch, cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the batter, and drop in the strawberries.
Place the skillet into the oven, and bake until puffed and golden, 20 to 25 minutes. Remove from the oven and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Skillet Strawberry Pancake
raw_recipe.description: This recipe is perfect for people who can't make good pancakes. Strawberries and the pancake batter are poured into a cast iron skillet and baked in this easy recipe.

video.description: Forgo the time-intensive stack of pancakes with this single-skillet extra large pancake for slicing to serve. All you need to do is put eggs, milk, vanilla, sugar, salt and flour into a blender. When pulsed smooth, pour into a hot cast iron skillet, dollop with fresh cut strawberries and bake in the oven until puffed, golden, and ready for copious amounts of syrup, powdered sugar, or both!

review.reviewBody: I used a mixture of strawberries and raspberries because I only had about a half cup of each. I used whole wheat white flour and buttermilk instead of whole milk. I used a round cake pan instead of a skillet because I don't have a cast iron skillet. This was really easy to make with my oldest son and when it was done, I let it cool for a couple minutes, then flipped it out and cut it into pieces with a pizza cutter. My kids had this with a little butter and homemade freezer jam. Huge hit!

Not having a cast-iron or ovenproof skillet, I melted 2T butter in my glass 8x8 Pyrex dish in the oven while mixing the ingredients. Followed nearly to the letter, only adding a few sprinkles of cinnamon to the batter as well as a drop of almond extract (in addition to the vanilla). After removing the dish with the melted butter, I sprinkled in some brown sugar and added the batter. I sprinkled some extra cinnamon and sugar to the top and it was perfectly puffed after 25 minutes (my oven runs hot, so I baked at 400). Make sure you let it rest for 5-10 minutes so it sets up well. The full cup of strawberries was a little much for our preference, so I'll simply use fewer next time. If you rinse and slice your strawberries immediately before adding to the batter, make sure they are completely dry, otherwise you'll have extra liquid floating on top. Love the puffy edges and the custardy texture. Served with homemade whipped cream and a dusting of powdered sugar. Delicious!

Great spin on a recipe I've been eating/cooking for many years! I always allow my cast iron skillet to heat up inside the oven as it's preheating. When the oven is up to temp and the batter is ready, I add the butter to the already hot skillet, swirl it around as it melts, then pour the batter in. I didn't have any strawberries on hand, so I used blueberries. Added a little cinnamon, and reduced sugar to 2 T. brown sugar. 

As kids, we knew these as "German Pancakes" -- they were one of our favorites. My son calls them "Puffy Pancakes." I typically cook them in a 10' cast iron skillet with varying ratios of eggs/flour/milk. (In a larger skillet, the edges really puff up and turn golden brown.) I use very little sugar in the batter, sometimes omitting it altogether. We've always liked to eat them with a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of powdered sugar. I also make a "french toast" version that has cinnamon and maple extract in the batter, served with a drizzle of maple syrup + sprinkle of powdered sugar on top.

Skillet pancakes are also called a Dutch Baby or a Hootin Annie. I made the Apple Dutch Baby this morning. It had skim milk instead of whole milk, because that’s what we had. I browned a whole apple’s worth of slices and picked out the 4 or 5 thinner ones that cooked to black instead of brown. (I ate them while the pancake was in the oven. ) Instead of a blender, I used my rotary hand beater. It turned out beautifully, and was delicious, light and sweet, but very filling.

I love this recipe! I followed the recommendations of some other reviewers of using only 2 eggs. I also like to add 1/4 almond flour and replace the vanilla extract for almond extract. Then finish with 1/4 cup sliced almonds in top of strawberries.

Used my 10" skillet. So 4 eggs, 1 cup of flour. Just add 25% more of each. Then I baked for the full 25 minutes.
No problems with a soft smooth pancake full of berries!

EXCELLENT and very easy. I enjoyed more than pancakes.
My First time I used 4 eggs, and added cinnamon to the batter. Pie was ready in 11 min. (but I live at 4700 altitude). I dusted the finished pie with butter dabs and powdered sugar. I'd say it's the quantity of 4 pancakes.
Next time I'll bake at 400 and stick with the 3 eggs and keep an eye on. Very versatile toppings.

I cut the recipe in half for a trial while my husband is away. (used one egg) I used apples with cinnamon. Checked it in 15 minutes and went another two .. Really easy to make and will keep making it. Excellent.

LOVE this recipe. I followed the recipe to a T the first time and give it 5 stars. I have since modified it using coconut oil instead of butter since we don't do much dairy, and I also throw in blueberries in addition to strawberries. I like it with the 3 eggs as it seems almost custardy. I double the recipe and bake it in a 9x13 pan. Any leftovers can be eaten cold straight from the fridge, almost like a dessert. Can't wait to try a savory version as others have suggested (no sugar and cheese added). Very versatile recipe.

Delicious! I used gluten-free baking flour hoping to have a family breakfast that my husband could also eat. We all loved it! In fact, my kids were disappointed that there was enough for seconds. 

I used 2 eggs as recommended. I added strawberries and half of a thinly sliced nectarine. This is definitely going to remain in the breakfast rotation! Thank you for the recipe

I followed the recipe and used a few blueberries and raspberries since that’s what I had on hand. I removed it from the oven after 20 minutes since the sides were all puffed up and golden brown. The top hadn’t browned, but it looked firm and I didn’t want to risk burning the sides. I let sit for 5 minutes outside the oven and let sizzle in the cast iron pan to make sure it was cooked through. It was sweet & like a firm custard. I would avoid using raspberries as they didn’t complement the flavor of the pancake and they faded to an unappealing color. I will make this again and bake it 1-2 min longer to see if the top browns.
This is an amazing recipe. I used blueberries instead of strawberries. It came out looking beautiful and a perfect melt in your mouth custard like consistency
Real good. Made with 2 eggs as people suggested and it wasn't dense. Easy to make and meal prep, too
premeasured everything. then my 5 year old grandson helped mixing with whisk instead of blender. He loved it! will make again.

Stick to 2 eggs. All else the same. Use glass pie pan and melt butter in oven while preheating. Good topped with Nutella. Also good with blueberries instead of strawberries topped with brown sugar cinnamon butter.
